newsitem.title: CANADA: TENNIS-RAYMOND OUSTS SCHULTZ-MCCARTHY IN QUEBEC.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAYMOND OUSTS SCHULTZ-MCCARTHY IN QUEBEC.

text.p: Fifth-seeded Lisa Raymond neutralised the vaunted serve of top-seeded defending champion Brenda Schultz-McCarthy on her way to a 6-0 7-6 (7-2) victory Friday in the quarter-finals of the $164,250 Bell Challenge.
Second-seeded Elena Likhovtseva of Russia was forced to a pair of tiebreakers but avoided Schultz-McCarthy's fate by prevailing 7-6 (7-4) 7-6 (7-1) over unseeded American Jolene Watanabe.
Two other leading seeds were also ousted.
Tami Whitlinger-Jones, ranked 80th, overcame fourth-seeded fellow-American Kimberly Po 1-6 6-4 7-5 to advance to Saturday's semifinals against 44th-ranked compatriot Raymond.
Unseeded Els Callens of Belgium eliminated sixth seed Florencia Labat of Argentina 6-4 6-4. Callens, ranked 73rd, will take on Likhovtseva in the other semifinal.

Blasting hard service returns and sizzling passing shots, Raymond got off to a fast start against the 11th-ranked Schultz-McCarthy. She won the first nine points of the match, including a service break in the second game.

The powerful Dutchwoman didn't hold serve until the second game of the second set. But then Raymond broke her at 2-1 and held serve for 4-1. Schultz-McCarthy battled back and forced a a tie-break after saving two match points trailing 5-6.
In the tiebreaker, Raymond's passing shots and Schultz-McCarthy's volley errors allowed the 23-year-old American to take a commanding 5-1 lead on her way winning 7-2.

"That's the best I've played this year," said Raymond after winning for the first time in six career matches against Schultz-McCarthy. Raymond, a two-time U.S. collegiate champion (1992-93) is looking for her first pro singles title.
"I think the key was I was able to break her serve early, that got her thinking. I was moving around a lot when she was serving, and I know for a fact that she doesn't like that."
"She kind of threw me off by where she was standing," Schultz-McCarthy said. "She had a good game plan. I guess she'd learned from losing to me before."

Schultz-McCarthy, who came to Quebec after European events in Filderstadt, Germany, and Zurich, Switzerland, admitted she might have been a little tired. "Sometimes you think you're superwoman but in reality you're not," she said.
